name: PAN-OS — Firewall Configuration Change by an Unexpected Administrator
description:
Attacker objective
A compromised or rogue administrator modifies the perimeter firewall — adding an allow rule, weakening a policy, or manipulating admin accounts — to enable access or evade defenses.

Attack logic
Firewall configuration is performed by a small, stable set of administrators. A configuration change by an administrator not seen in the historical window is anomalous on an internet-edge firewall.

Why this detection works
PAN-OS CONFIG logs fully attribute each change to an admin; a new-terms model auto-baselines the known admin set and fires on a genuinely new one.

False positives
Onboarding of a new legitimate firewall admin.

Tuning
Allowlist verified new admins; the history window auto-baselines over time.

Required telemetry
PAN-OS CONFIG logs (admin, cmd, path, result).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. admin = the account; path/cmd = what changed (watch for security rulebase and management-user changes).
2. Confirm the admin was authorised and review the specific change against change control.
false_positives: Onboarding of a new legitimate firewall admin.
